figures.caption: Figure 2. Spectator architecture and training. The encoder maps recent fMRI observations to a fast state ft and aggregates fast-state history into a slow state ut, forming the latent state st = [ft;ut]. A linear predictor evolves this state forward with multimodal movie features. During joint-embedding training, multistep predicted states are aligned with stop-gradient target states inferred from future observations by an exponential moving average (EMA) target encoder Ē. A frozen linear probe (readout) maps latent states to whole-cortex fMRI strictly for evaluation (Sec. 4.1).

Table 1. Overview of BrainStateBench. Each task evaluates a model’s predicted latent states via a frozen linear probe and reports variance explained (%) in the target. Forecast measures multi-step prediction without new observations, Updating measures state revision as new observations arrive, and State measures state inference across repeated trials of the same stimulus.

Figure 3. Latent state governs near-term forecasts while the stimulus dominates longer horizons. Decomposing 180 s Spectator rollouts on held-out Algonauts recordings (Sec. D): (a) variance share of the latent-state versus stimulus component over the 60 s rollout; (b, c) Forecast accuracy when omitting a component or swapping it across time or individuals.

Figure 4. Stimuli drive shared sensory and narrative-processing cortex, whereas latent state improves prediction cortex-wide. Forecast gain from adding (a) the stimulus to state-only and (b) the latent state to stimulus-only predictions on the left hemisphere (100 Schaefer regions [34]; top lateral regions labeled via NeuroQuery [8]). (c) Mean gain across 1,000-parcel tertiles of inter-subject correlation.

Table 4. Learned slow state, linear operators, and two-stage training drive Spectator’s performance. Changes relative to full 180 s Spectator (16.0, 5.5, 20.3, 0.349; Tab. 2), in percentage points for BrainStateBench tasks and ∆r for correlation (default → ablated).
Table 5. Hyperparameters and training settings of Spectator across model components and training stages.

Table 6. Summary of baseline configurations on Algonauts. Scoring readout specifies how model outputs or states map to parcel predictions, and the final column specifies how unrevealed intermediate steps are handled during Updating. HCP adaptations are described in Sec. B.6.

Figure 5. Spectator uniquely scales with multi-minute neural history. Performance on (a) Forecast, (b) State, and (c) Updating across fMRI history lengths from 7.5 s to 180 s. Baselines plateau or degrade at longer contexts, whereas Spectator improves steadily across all three tasks (dashed lines: stimulus-only models without fMRI input).

Figure 6. Spectator leads at every forecast horizon and observation budget (180 s fMRI history). Left, Middle: Forecast and State across lead times, showing informative state predictions well beyond initial steps. Right: Updating versus number of intermediate observations supplied during the 60 s rollout (default: 4, bold).

Table 8. Spectator’s gains at 120 s and 180 s are statistically significant across all baselines and metrics. Paired differences (Spectator minus baseline, in percentage points for BrainStateBench tasks and ∆r for correlation) with 95% confidence intervals from 2,000 paired bootstrap resamples over held-out recordings.

Table 10. Spectator also leads on standard metrics at multi-minute horizons. Parcel-wise Pearson r and whole-cortex global r averaged over steps 1–20 or 1–40, and 20-step segment identification accuracy Cls@Top10 (%, chance 0.05%, best and second best per history length).

Table 13. Shared linear probe transfers zero-shot to unseen HCP individuals, requiring minimal calibration. Scores (%) on the held-out fourth recording of the unseen HCP individuals (35 for Forecast, 34 for Updating; 180 s history) when adding a ridge correction fitted on the first 1–15 min of each individual’s first recording. Gains are paired differences computed before rounding with 95% confidence intervals.

Table 14. Encoder design governs near-term accuracy while latent rollout training sustains long-horizon forecasts. Change in Forecast (percentage points relative to full Spectator) across the full minute (0–60 s), near future (0–7.5 s), and far future (30–60 s).

Figure 7. Spectator stays stable for five minutes, whereas its Transformer variant diverges. (a) Per-step Forecast accuracy over 5 min. (b) Mean scores (%) within each horizon interval. Stimulus-only Spectator and TRIBE v2 [7] receive no fMRI history; the Transformer variant replaces both gϕ and pθ (Tab. 4), and its trajectory continues below the plotted range.

Figure 8. Forecasts rely primarily on transmodal default-mode and control networks. (a) Top 100 input parcels ranked by GradientSHAP attribution of past fMRI observations onto Spectator’s forecasts, colored by functional network [47]. (b) Network breakdown, led by default-mode (38) and frontoparietal control (20) regions.

Figure 9. Spectator learns stable, multi-timescale latent dynamics. (a) Relative variance shares of the initial-state and stimulus components across forecast horizons. (b) Normalized fMRI impulse response to a single-step stimulus perturbation across responsive parcels, peaking near 3 s. (c) Survival distribution of eigenmode 1/e decay times across all 2,048 latent modes, with 21.7% persisting beyond 30 s.

Figure 10. About 100 of the 2,048 latent dimensions recover 90% of Forecast and State. Scores on (a) Forecast, (b) State, and (c) Updating when each individual’s probe reads only the top principal components of the predicted latent states, or a random subspace of the same size. Spectator itself is unchanged. Dashed lines mark the probe on all 2,048 dimensions (Tab. 2).

Figure 11. Spectator scales effectively from limited per-individual fMRI. Performance on (a) Forecast, (b) State, and (c) Updating on held-out fMRI (180 s history) across matched nested subsets of the 118 training episodes per individual (Spectator retrained end-to-end at each budget). Dashed horizontal lines mark the linear forecaster trained on 100% of the episodes.

Table 16. Spectator leads across all metrics at every training-data budget. Scores (%) on held-out fMRI (180 s history) for matched nested subsets of the 118 training episodes (46.6 h per individual). Spectator is retrained end-to-end on each subset; the linear forecaster fits either to recorded fMRI or to forecasts generated by the Spectator teacher trained on the same subset. Bold marks the best score at each data budget.

Table 17. Supervising downstream models with Spectator’s trajectories yields significant gains across all students. Scores (%) on real held-out fMRI (180 s history) and paired differences (percentage points, computed before rounding) relative to each student’s realtarget baseline with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Equal mix averages recorded fMRI and Spectator forecast targets; “+” augments the preceding target set. Shading and bold mark the best setting per student.
